title: Apple Scrambles for DRAM, CXMT Reportedly Rejects Negotiations
gist: Apple is scrambling to secure DRAM (mainly Micron LPDDR5X) weeks before the iPhone 18/iPhone Ultra launch, and when it tried to negotiate discounted LPDDR5X pricing from China's CXMT, CXMT refused because Chinese hyperscalers and AI labs are already absorbing its full output at market rates — an early sign that supplier leverage over even Apple is shifting in a tightening DRAM market.

insights.claim: With less than six weeks until the launch of the iPhone 18 series and the iPhone Ultra, Apple and its assemblers are rushing to place DRAM orders to secure new supplies amid the current DRAM shortage, according to Tim Culpan's Culpium newsletter.
insights.speaker: B
insights.so_what: Even Apple, one of the world's largest supply-chain operators, is exposed to DRAM shortage risk right before a flagship launch — a leading indicator that DRAM tightness is severe enough to threaten major OEM launch timelines.
insights.quote: With less than six weeks until the launch of the iPhone 18 series and the iPhone Ultra, assemblers are rushing to place DRAM orders to secure new supplies.
insights.locator: According to Tim Culpan's Culpium newsletter

insights.claim: Apple primarily relies on Micron for DRAM, whose LPDDR5X memory is used across a range of devices and is the main memory source for the next-generation iPhone, with SK hynix and Samsung as secondary suppliers.
insights.speaker: B
insights.so_what: Confirms Micron as Apple's primary LPDDR5X counterparty for iPhone 18 — Micron's allocation decisions and pricing are the key variable to watch for Apple's launch supply risk.
insights.quote: The Cupertino-based giant primarily relies on DRAM from Micron, whose LPDDR5X memory is used in a range of devices and is the main source for the next-generation iPhone.
insights.locator: The Cupertino-based giant primarily relies on DRAM from Micron

themes.theme: CXMT negotiation and shifting supplier leverage

insights.claim: Apple has reportedly entered negotiations with Chinese memory maker CXMT for LPDDR5X memory needed for its current product lineup, attempting to negotiate a lower price likely due to the volume it plans to purchase, but CXMT rejected the proposed lower price.
insights.speaker: B
insights.so_what: Apple failing to extract a volume discount from a Chinese memory supplier is a concrete, named data point of Apple's weakened buyer leverage in the current memory market.
insights.quote: Apple attempted to negotiate better pricing with CXMT, likely due to the volume it plans to purchase, but CXMT rejected the proposed lower price.
insights.locator: Interestingly, another report has surfaced about Apple's efforts

insights.claim: This is described as one of the first instances where negotiation power lies with the suppliers rather than the buyer, since CXMT is producing one of the world's most in-demand commodities and is offering it at market rates without discounts.
insights.speaker: B
insights.so_what: A regime change in buyer-supplier power dynamics for DRAM is a signal that memory suppliers (CXMT, and by extension Samsung, SK hynix, Micron) may be able to hold firmer pricing even against their largest customers.
insights.quote: This is one of the first instances where negotiation power lies with the suppliers, as CXMT is producing one of the world's most in-demand commodities and is offering it at market rates without discounts.
insights.locator: This is one of the first instances where negotiation power

insights.claim: Chinese hyperscalers, neo clouds, and AI labs are buying up all the available DRAM CXMT manufactures, so any output CXMT could offer Apple is already reserved for Chinese customers willing to pay full market price rather than seeking discounts.
insights.speaker: B
insights.so_what: Domestic Chinese AI/cloud demand is directly crowding out even Apple's ability to source discounted DRAM from a Chinese supplier — a channel to watch for how China's AI buildout is redirecting its own domestic chip supply away from export customers.
insights.quote: Chinese companies, including hyperscalers, neo clouds, and AI labs, are buying up all the available DRAM that CXMT is manufacturing.
insights.locator: Chinese companies, including hyperscalers, neo clouds, and AI labs

insights.claim: As DRAM becomes even scarcer next year, this supplier-side leverage in the memory supply chain is likely to increase further, and it remains unclear whether Apple has accepted CXMT's standard market prices.
insights.speaker: B
insights.so_what: Signals continued upward DRAM pricing pressure into next year is the base case — relevant for modeling Apple's and other OEMs' bill-of-materials cost trajectory beyond the current iPhone cycle.
insights.quote: As DRAM becomes even scarcer next year, this leverage in the supply chain is likely to increase in favor of DRAM manufacturers.
insights.locator: As DRAM becomes even scarcer next year
